projectSummary: This is a project under the CERF-funded anticipatory action (AA) framework for cyclones in Madagascar. projectSummary: The primary objective of this project is to reduce the impact of the below average rains on pastoral and agro‑pastoral households in Oromia and Somali regions. The project will support households to protect livelihoods and strengthen food security. Livestock health services will be expanded through vaccination of 2.8 million animals and treatment for drought‑affected households. Refresher training for Community Animal Health Workers will improve disease surveillance and response capacity. To boost crop production, 61 tonnes of climate‑resilient maize seeds will be distributed. Unconditional cash transfers of USD 100 will help households meet urgent needs and prevent negative coping strategies. Overall, the project targets 247,000 people, including 57,305 women, 56,315 men, 66,690 girls, 66,690 boys, and including 43,472 persons with disabilities.
projectTitle: Emergency Rapid Drought Response support to save lives and livelihoods in Somali and Oromia Regions of Ethiopia

projectSummary: The primary objective of this project is to deliver essential Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) and Nutrition services to communities affected by below-average rainfall across Somali, Oromia, and South Ethiopia regions. UNICEF support will rehabilitate critical water systems, provide emergency WASH supplies, and strengthen hygiene and risk reduction activities to address acute water shortages. Under the nutrition component, UNICEF will provide lifesaving screening and treatment for severe acute malnutrition, distribute Ready to Use Therapeutic Food (RUTF), and deliver maternal, infant, and young child nutrition counselling. Micronutrient supplementation for children 6–59 months and for pregnant and breastfeeding women and girls will further strengthen nutritional outcomes. Overall, the project targets 85,710 people, including 32,460 women, 20,251 men, 15,750 girls, 17,249 boys, and including 5,000 persons with disabilities, prioritizing the most drought affected and high-risk communities.
projectTitle: Life Saving Wash and Nutrition Rapid Response to Drought-affected communities in Oromia, Somali and South Ethiopia Regions

projectSummary: The primary objective of this project is to provide life‑saving health and nutrition services to affected populations. WHO and partners will assist over 130,000 people with essential health care, outbreak response, and mobile health services in hotspot and hard‑to‑reach areas. Support will include treatment for outbreak‑prone diseases, including cholera, and last‑mile delivery of medical and nutrition supplies to public health facilities serving displaced and host communities. projectTitle: Emergency health assistance to affected by drought in Oromia, Somali and South Ethiopia Regions

projectSummary: The main goal of this project is to provide urgent assistance to vulnerable people affected by below-average rainfall in Somali, Oromia, and South Ethiopia through multi‑purpose cash Assistance. WFP uses this allocation to deliver unconditional cash transfers that enable households to meet their immediate food and non‑food needs, stabilize consumption, and protect remaining livelihoods and assets. The monthly transfer value of USD 98 is provided for three months follows nationally endorsed MPCA guidance and supports households facing rapidly deteriorating conditions. This project targets 18,990 people, of whom 4,653 are women, 4,842 are men, 4,653 are girls, 4,842 are boys, and of whom 2,090 are persons with disabilities.
projectTitle: Rapid response to Ethiopia January 2026 drought through multi-purpose cash assistance

WHO’s strategic response is also aligned with the HCT Flash Appeal and “Lebanon Response Plan-2026". The project targets 2,352 affected people with lifesaving activities in the Health sector.
projectTitle: Emergency Support for Trauma Care Kits and Hospitalization Coverage Amid Escalating Hostilities in Lebanon (2026)

projectSummary: This project provides life‑saving assistance to conflict‑affected people in Lebanon – displaced Lebanese and Syrians – through two complementary modalities: daily meals for displaced populations residing in collective shelters, and emergency multi-purpose cash assistance for families in areas where markets continue to function. The objective is to ensure uninterrupted access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food during displacement, reduce harmful coping strategies, and help stabilize households as the situation evolves. The project directly targets 32,364 affected people with life-saving activities in the Food Security (Food Assistance) sector.
projectTitle: Life-saving cash and meals assistance to conflict-affected people in Lebanon

projectSummary: This FAO project is part of the collective anticipatory action (AA) framework for drought in Mauritania.  The main objective of this AA project is to provide agricultural assistance to vulnerable communities at risk of severe drought across the Guidimakha region of Mauritania. Through this project, FAO provides cash transfers and drought resistant agricultural inputs, promotes forage conservation techniques and distributes livestock feed among other activities to ensure that communities are protected from and prepared for impending severe drought conditions. The project provides life-saving assistance to an estimated 12,100 people, including 3,640 women, 4,020 men, and 4,440 children.
projectTitle: Actions anticipatoires pour réduire l’impact des sécheresses sur les populations les plus à risque dans la région du Guidimakha

projectSummary: This WFP project is part of the collective anticipatory action (AA) framework for drought in Mauritania. The main objective of this AA project is to provide food security assistance to vulnerable communities at risk of severe drought across the Guidimakha region of Mauritania. Through this project, WFP provides multipurpose cash transfers, among other activities to ensure that communities are protected from and prepared for impending severe drought conditions. The project provides life-saving assistance to an estimated 34,449 people, including 8,784 women, 8,440 men,  and 17,225 children, including 584 people with disabilities.
projectTitle: Anticipatory action and early response to mitigate drought impacts on vulnerable households

projectSummary: This UNICEF project is part of the collective anticipatory action (AA) framework for drought in Mauritania. The main objective of this AA project is to provide nutrition and WASH assistance to vulnerable communities at risk of severe drought across the Guidimakha region of Mauritania. Through this project, UNICEF provides Multi-micronutrient (MNP) supplementation for children, emergency storage and treatment of drinking water, as well as education on good hygiene practice, among other activities to ensure that communities are protected from and prepared for impending severe drought conditions. The project provides life-saving assistance to an estimated 64,750 people, including 31,372 women, 11,152 men, and 21,865 children, including 7,580 persons with disabilities.
projectTitle: Actions anticipatoires dans la nutrition et la WASH pour la sécheresse dans la région de Guidimahka en Mauritanie

projectSummary: This IOM project is part of the collective anticipatory action (AA) framework for drought in Mauritania.  The main objective of this AA project is to provide protection assistance to vulnerable communities at risk of severe drought across the Guidimakha region of Mauritania. Through this project, IOM harmonizes and simplifies alert messages, ensuring the accessibility of communications of impending drought, increasing the awareness amongst the most vulnerable and isolated communities. projectSummary: This UNICEF project is part of window 1 of the collective anticipatory action (AA) framework for drought in Chad. The main objective of this AA project is to launch a malnutrition screening campaign in each of the three priority departments to enable effective geographic targeting based on village-level data for the multi-sectoral assistance package delivered by partners. Through this project, UNICEF conducts extensive malnutrition screening of approximately 160,000 children (including about 90,000 girls) under the age of five in prioritized areas to identify cases of acute malnutrition and provide adequate referrals for treatment.
projectTitle: Appui au dépistage précoce de la malnutrition aiguë dans les trois départements priorisés par l’action anticipatoire 2026 au niveau des provinces du Kanem et du Barh-El-Gazel.

projectSummary: This FAO project is part of the collective anticipatory action (AA) framework for drought in Chad. The main objective of this AA project is to protect and strengthen the agricultural and pastoral livelihoods of vulnerable communities in the provinces of Kanem, Bahr-el-Ghazal, and Batha who are at high risk of severe drought in the upcoming June-September season. Through this project, FAO provides anticipatory agricultural assistance, including the distribution of climate-resilient seeds and rehabilitation of wells equipped with solar-powered systems in order to sustainably improve access to water for agricultural purposes. The project provides life-saving assistance to 63,000 people, including 5,249 women, 5,249 men, 52,502 children, including 6,300 persons with disabilities.
projectTitle: Actions anticipatoires pour la résilience agropastorale et la sécurité alimentaire des ménages vulnérables dans le Kanem, le Bahr-el-Ghazal et le Batha face aux impacts de la sécheresse.

projectSummary: This WFP project is part of the collective anticipatory action (AA) framework for drought in Chad. Through this project, WFP provides lifesaving early warning messages and anticipatory cash assistance to 56,952 people, including 14,808 women, 13,668 men and 28.476 children.
projectTitle: Action anticipatoire pour atténuer l’impact de la sécheresse sur les populations vulnérables au Tchad

projectSummary: This project delivers immediate life-saving food assistance to conflict-affected and severely food-insecure people in Akobo County, Jonglei State, while enabling the wider inter-agency humanitarian response through common logistics services in some of South Sudan’s most access-constrained operational environments. It directly targets 92,811 most vulnerable conflict-affected people in Akobo (Women: 14,850, Girls: 35,268, Men: 12,065, Boys: 30,628) with emergency in-kind food assistance during the peak lean season to prevent further deterioration in food consumption and acute food insecurity outcomes. Under the common services component, WFP, through the Logistics Cluster, provides critical inter-agency logistics support to facilitate the movement of life-saving humanitarian relief items into hard-to-reach operational areas in Akobo, including support to the broader multisectoral CERF response.
projectTitle: Emergency food assistance and humanitarian logistics support for conflict-affected populations in Akobo and high-severity counties in South Sudan

projectSummary: This project uses CERF funding to scale up integrated assistance in Akobo County, Jonglei State, and Upper Nile State, complementing ongoing response in Uror, Nyirol, and Abiemnhom counties. The additional funding allows UNICEF and partners to expand life-saving Health, Nutrition, WASH, Child Protection and Gender-Based Violence programming. The response increases access to essential services and reduce preventable morbidity, mortality, and protection risks among vulnerable populations. projectSummary: This WHO project supports the Government of Uganda’s response to the Ebola outbreak to prevent further transmission within Uganda and across the region. The project enhances healthcare preparedness through support to health facilities, community-based surveillance systems, early detection, contact tracing, case management, referral systems, ambulance services, and coordination with the Ministry of Health and District Local Governments. projectSummary: The main objective of this project is to reduce immediate protection and shelter-related risks for people affected by the earthquakes in La Guaira through critical protection services, case management, specialized referrals, core relief item distributions, and shelter support for safe service delivery spaces. This UNHCR project provides protection profiling, case management, psychosocial support and safe referrals for people with specific needs; distributes essential household items to earthquake-affected families; and installs temporary shelters and prefabricated units to create safe, dignified and accessible spaces for protection services and assistance. The project provides life-saving assistance to 12,000 people, including 4,856 women, 3,829 men, 3,315 children, and including 748 people with disabilities.
projectTitle: Life-Saving protection, core relief items and shelter assistance for people affected by the earthquakes in La Guaira, Venezuela

projectSummary: The main objective of this project is to provide vital Sexual and Reproductive Health services and Gender-Based Violence response services to vulnerable women and girls affected by the June 2026 earthquakes in La Guaira, Miranda, and the Capital District. This UNFPA project provides mobile prenatal and SRH care alongside essential medicines and emergency reproductive health kits; delivers confidential, survivor-centred GBV case management and psychosocial support through fixed, mobile, and remote services; and distributes menstrual hygiene and dignity kits with information on GBV risk mitigation and available services. The project provides life-saving assistance to 55,599 people, including 42,158 women, 4,396 men, and 9,045 children.

projectSummary: The main objective of this project is to ensure timely access to adequate food for populations affected by the earthquakes in Venezuela, through emergency food assistance. This WFP project identifies and verifies earthquake-affected households for assistance; distributes emergency food rations to meet their essential food needs; and establishes community feedback mechanisms to receive, address, follow up on, and close beneficiary concerns. The project delivers life-saving assistance to 12,800 people, including 3,910 women, 3,032 men, and 5,858 children.
projectTitle: Restoring Food Security for Communities Affected by Venezuela's Twin Earthquakes
